links.outcome: Agreement between question and response readability under four prompting strategies (quadratic-weighted kappa)
links.effect: External calculator-guided prompting gave the highest agreement (Gemini 3 kappa=0.94; GPT 5.2 kappa=0.90). Formula-informed prompting was intermediate. Semantic inference agreed poorly. Factual accuracy stayed above 98% for GPT 5.2 and Gemini 3.
links.quote: The external calculator-guided strategy produced the strongest alignment in readability across models, achieving the highest agreement (Gemini 3: κ=0.94; GPT 5.2: κ=0.90), while maintaining favorable computational efficiency.

unlisted_practices: Using an external readability calculator in the prompting pipeline to match response readability to the user's question readability

screen.practice: reading-level constraints and readability prompting strategies
screen.reason: The study tests different prompt-engineering guardrails/strategies (formula-informed prompt, semantic inference, external calculator-guided prompt) versus baseline to align LLM responses with patient readability requirements while assessing factual accuracy.
